events.event: the file does not reach the Userscripts folder on the first try (wrong folder, unsure which, or saved again)
events.observable: the narration says the file went to another folder, had to be moved or saved again, or that the folder was a worry
events.rests_on: HW1 A4 says the remembered folder costs nothing, for another destination; nothing on the save sheet says which folder is right

events.event: after the reload the owner is unsure whether the script is installed, and looks for or waits for the button
events.observable: the narration says they did not know whether it had worked, looked for the button or reloaded again
events.rests_on: progress finding at step 10: nothing on the page says the script is there until the 初稿 button appears

events.event: the owner cannot find the 初稿 button on the SpeedGrader page (another control covers it, or it is mistaken for one)
events.observable: the narration or a screenshot shows a search for the button, or it hidden
events.rests_on: its place (top right, 72 px down) was measured on the mock page, not on the real SpeedGrader

events.event: the first read ends in a red line instead of the counts (a refusal, a lost login, an answer of Canvas the script did not expect)
events.observable: a screenshot or the narration shows a red line in the sheet at the first check
events.rests_on: the real Canvas has not been tried; the guards (points total, grading type, group, anonymous, moderated) and the field names are assumptions

events.event: the sheet says that more than half of the students' files do not match (the file ids mean something else than the script assumes)
events.observable: the sheet shows the line about the file check and its button
events.rests_on: the middle number of Canvas's file names is assumed to be the attachment id (about 80% sure)

events.event: the counts differ from the numbers in the chat and the owner stops to work out why
events.observable: the narration says the numbers were not what the chat said, or they compared and puzzled
events.rests_on: skipped, absent and unchecked counts depend on the real course (graded students, a missing-submission zero, the two emailed students)

events.event: the counts and the main button are on one screen, with no scrolling
events.observable: a screenshot of the sheet shows the counts and the main button together
events.rests_on: docs/predictions/draft-publish-first-run.measured.json: the main button is in view in every state, the footer does not scroll

events.event: the owner does not see why only one student is written the first time
events.observable: the narration says they did not understand the one-student step, or tapped expecting all
events.rests_on: the posting line and the button label ('先试写 1 位') say it; the owner has no habit for it yet

events.event: the owner does not read the first student's preview to the end (it needs a scroll) or skips it
events.observable: the narration says they did not read it, or a screenshot shows it unscrolled at the tap
events.rests_on: measured: the scrolling part of the sheet is 1.2 screens with the clipped preview (3.9 before the clip); a reader taps when the button is in view

events.event: the owner hesitates at the confirmation (reads it twice, or cancels and starts again)
events.observable: the narration says they hesitated or cancelled
events.rests_on: an irreversible write that the student sees at once; the dialog is native text

events.event: the trial write ends with a red line instead of 试写完成
events.observable: a screenshot or the narration shows a failure after the trial
events.rests_on: the first real write on the real Canvas: permissions, the rubric assessment form, the rate limit

events.event: after the reload the owner cannot find the written student in SpeedGrader
events.observable: the narration says they searched for the student
events.rests_on: the sheet lists in the order of the names; SpeedGrader's own order is assumed to be the same

events.event: the owner takes the result line as the check and does not look for a proof elsewhere
events.observable: the narration does not mention verifying the write by other means than looking at the student
events.rests_on: the line says the write was read back and matched; the verifiers find no gap there

events.event: SpeedGrader does not show the written comments at first (the rubric is collapsed or the comments need a tap)
events.observable: the narration says the comments were not visible at first
events.rests_on: how SpeedGrader shows free-form criterion comments on a phone is not known

events.event: the owner finds a deduction or a comment they think is wrong in the first student
events.observable: the narration says something looked wrong
events.rests_on: an unreviewed machine draft; HW1's first pass had errors

events.event: the comment layout (tags such as [Q5b-gen], long keys) looks odd or too long to the owner
events.observable: the narration says the comments looked strange or too long
events.rests_on: the layout is TapGrade's, which the owner knows; keys are long

events.event: the owner stops after the look and does not write the rest in the same sitting
events.observable: the narration or the chat says they stopped
events.rests_on: depends on what they see in L2

events.event: the owner does not find the way back to the pending write (the button reads 初稿·已试写)
events.observable: the narration says they did not know what to do next
events.rests_on: the label and the line 'you wrote only <name> last time' are meant to bring the goal back

events.event: the counts after the trial surprise the owner (the written student counts as already the draft)
events.observable: the narration says the numbers were not what they expected
events.rests_on: the count of 'already the draft' is 1 at this point

events.event: the owner hesitates at the second confirmation
events.observable: the narration says they hesitated
events.rests_on: after looking at one student the decision is made; the dialog is the same kind

events.event: the long write ends with one or more failed students
events.observable: the footer line shows a failure count above 0
events.rests_on: the first run at scale on the real Canvas: rate limits, permission quirks, a student with no enrolment

events.event: the page is interrupted during the long write (the phone locks, another app, a reload)
events.observable: the narration says the write was interrupted or the button read 初稿·未完
events.rests_on: 1 to 3 minutes on a phone; Safari may suspend a tab that is not in view

events.event: the owner compares the final numbers with the chat and finds a mismatch they have to explain
events.observable: the narration says the totals did not match what the chat said
events.rests_on: 59 was the plan; skipped, unchecked and held counts depend on the real course

events.event: the final line is understood at the first reading
events.observable: the narration does not say they re-read it
events.rests_on: one line with three numbers and the read-back statement

events.event: the owner does not understand Canvas's own error text for a failed student
events.observable: the narration says the message was unclear (only if a run had failures)

events.observable: the narration says they understood and continued (only if a write was interrupted)

scoring.coding: the transcriber codes each event from the narration and the screenshots using the event and observable columns only, writes the outcomes file, and only then runs the script; the p column is not read while coding

outcome.1: the observable condition is met by the narration or the screenshots
outcome.0: the event's segment is narrated or shown and the condition is not met
outcome.null: the segment is neither narrated nor shown: the event is not scored (conditional chains: S5 to S8)

scoring.brier: mean over scored events of (p - o)^2, against the constant forecast at the mean p and against 0.5; also per basis and per segment
scoring.kendall: not scored unless 4 comparable segments have a measured duration; with S2 to S4 only, it is not
scoring.onsets: narrated losses within two steps of a predicted onset at B = 3 (none are predicted at B = 3: every chain peaks at 3 slots), B = 2 and B = 4 as registered
scoring.p02be: the observed rate of events whose steps carry a verifier finding against events whose steps carry none; unregistered frictions; false findings
scoring.owner_leaves: if you can: a few lines written right after, in your own words, of what slowed you, what you re-read and what surprised you; and screenshots with the clock. Nothing else. If you cannot, say so: the screenshots alone score the events they show.

P-02be.claim: a chain can pass by omission: the silence of the verifiers does not mean a step is smooth
shown_on_this_pass_if: an unregistered friction sits at a step where no verifier fired
a finding sits at a step the narration calls smooth

load model.claim: the chains, written from the code, find where the owner is slowed
falsified_if: the events at steps with a finding occur no more often than the events at steps without one, over at least 15 scored events

the publisher's own assumptions.claim: the first real run reveals what the mock could not
shown_if: I4, I5, T4 or W4 occur: the real Canvas answered something the script did not expect

limits: written by the author of the publisher, of the fixture and of this generator, with no second reader, and after the first build had already been sent to the owner
the weights are ordinal and uncalibrated (P-67a1); amounts are guesses; 20 of the 29 probabilities are guesses and 5 predict that nothing goes wrong
the sheet was measured on a mock Canvas in headless Chromium at 390x844 touch with this container's fonts, not on an iPhone, not on the real SpeedGrader, whose own controls may cover the 初稿 button
the owner is ill, and this is a pass under that condition, which the model does not know about
if the owner ran any version before this registration was pushed, this registration is void for that run: the outcomes may be coded but are post hoc
S5 to S8 are conditional chains: their events are scored only if the segment happens
